[b]A Response[/b]

Julian looks at the printout of the communication received from Romarii by the State Department earlier that morning. Sipping on his morning coffee, he had been a long day of meetings with various military commanders and reassuring liberal senators and House members of the war plan. After this "emergency" meeting, he also had to go to Montfleour tonight. 

"What the f*ck is this?" Julian blurts out loud, Ashveld in the corner, snickering from reading the same letter, a fresh bottle of water in hand

Ashveld looks at Eklebloom. "Mary, you aren't messing with us, this is actually what they sent us...?"

"No, Mr Vice President, this is the exact text of the message I received this morning. They also posted...posted this in their local news." Mary says, struggling to contain laughter herself

"Are you SERIOUS? I mean, Mary, Julian...LOOK AT THIS," Ashveld says, not even pretending to be serious anymore, laughing, bursting out from his mouth as he accidentally drops the water bottle he was holding

"THEY WRITE LIKE A CHILD. AND THIS FROM...THERE PRESIDENT? DIRECTLY? he literally has sections in all caps. HE SENT A DIPLPOMATIC MESSAGE WITH RANDOM SECTIONS IN ALL CAPS

DOES HE THINK THIS SOCIAL MEDIA?"

Julian looks at his Vice President, glaring 

"Kori, compose yourself. We have work to do. Eklebloom. Its your job to respond to this. Be mature, please."

"Of course, Mr President."

________________________________
[b]Statement in Response[/b]

From: Acting Secretary of State, Mary Eikelboom

To: Mario Mario and whom it may concern within the Romariian Government.

Acting in my role as the duly appointed acting Secretary of State. I am writing this message to inform you that we completely reject your request for an extended deadline on our ultimatum, or removal of certain terms, nor will my government cease any efforts to prepare for the liberation of the islands and your removal from the presidency.

I want to remind President Mario Mario that he is the head of state of his nation, the leading representative to his people, and the message that my department received was, in the politest possible way, extremely disrespectful. And has soured my government's hope that a peaceful resolution to the conflict may still be possible. In my 20 years of service to my nation within the State Department and as a representative, I have never before seen an official communication so disrespectful and aggressive, and so lacking of professionalism and courtesy. 

My government is no longer willing to communicate on this issue. Unfortunately, President Mario's fitful cycles of lashing out show us that there is no genuine willingness from your government for peace or stability in the region, and prove that President Mario is an unstable actor who would surely make any future discussion on peace a useless endeavour.

You have our demands. Wuloosyan Forces will be be conducting military operations, including landings on the colonial islands, within weeks. It is now your choice.

Truly, Acting Secretary of State Mary Eikelboom

Cecilia drove her to the Velnaz Hospital the night things got bad. It started with headaches that medication couldnt touch, then graduated to fatigue and nausea over the course of a few weeks. That night, All she did was walk down the hall- she had gone to get a glass of water. Then the headache became a screaming in her ears, like a thousand voices. The lights were blinding, and her senses betrayed her before she collapsed. From Velnaz she was moved to the coast, a private residence outside of Attika. Cecilia made the trip with her that night, with Marniy to arrive in the morning. The doctors hadn't found the cause of her sickness , but she slept through the night in Attika, however fitful.

Marniy arrived at the wrong time- after Elena had woken up. She heard the howling from outside and walked in to find her sobbing. Bloody lips from biting, crumpled on the floor, wrapped in blankets from the bed. Marniy rushed to her side, and gently took her daughter's hands. She looked at Cecilia with a grim expression.
